title: EPCIS — Electronic Product Code Information Services
objectives: Understand EPCIS via a real-life analogy
Distinguish the 5 event types + CBV vocabularies
Design queries via EPCIS 2.0 REST APIs
Publish + subscribe to events across parties
Fit EPCIS into a Flutter app + backend architecture

sections.markdown:
**Think of EPCIS as the log format + query language for supply-chain events.**

Every physical event (packed, shipped, received, dispensed, disaggregated) that touches a GS1 identifier gets recorded as an EPCIS event — a structured JSON (or XML) with WHO, WHAT, WHEN, WHERE, WHY. Parties store their own events + expose them via a standard REST API so other parties (regulators, downstream partners) can query.

- **Event = a fact about a physical thing at a moment** — 'at 2026-03-10 14:23 UTC, SGTIN X was shipped from GLN Y to GLN Z on PO 12345.'
- **5 event types** — Object, Aggregation, Transaction, Transformation, Association (2.0).
- **CBV (Core Business Vocabulary)** — standardized values for `bizStep` (shipping, receiving, packing, dispense, destroy) + `disposition` (in_transit, in_progress, sold, destroyed).
- **Master data** — separate GLN + product + party metadata shared alongside events.
- **Query API** — get events matching filters (SGTIN, time, GLN, bizStep) via EPCIS Query Language.
- **Subscribe** — long-poll or webhook for real-time event delivery.

**Why EPCIS is the backbone of every serious modern supply-chain / pharma app:** without it, each party stores in its own DB + no interop = fragmented trace. With EPCIS, cross-party queries answer 'where is this batch?' in seconds. GS1 EPCIS 2.0 (2022+) moves to JSON-LD + REST + open standard — dramatically easier to implement in modern stacks including Flutter.

**EPCIS (Electronic Product Code Information Services)** is a GS1 standard for capturing + sharing supply-chain events. **Model:** an event describes a physical activity involving one or more EPCs (SGTINs, SSCCs). **Event types (5):** Object, Aggregation, Transaction, Transformation, Association. **Vocabularies:** CBV (Core Business Vocabulary) standardizes bizStep + disposition values. **API:** EPCIS 2.0 defines REST endpoints for capture + query + subscribe using JSON-LD. **Governance:** ISO/IEC 19987 + GS1 standards.

## EPCIS 2.0 REST API surface

sections.code:
# Capture — POST an event
curl -X POST https://epcis.example.com/capture \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/ld+json' \
  -d @event.json

# Query events
curl 'https://epcis.example.com/queries/all?EQ_bizStep=shipping&GE_eventTime=2026-03-01T00:00:00Z'

# Subscribe (webhook)
curl -X POST https://epcis.example.com/queries/all/subscriptions \
  -d '{"destination":"https://mycallback.example.com/hook", "schedule":"immediate"}'

# Get specific event by ID
curl 'https://epcis.example.com/events/{eventID}'

# Get all events for an EPC
curl 'https://epcis.example.com/eventTypes/ObjectEvent/events?EQ_MATCH_epc=urn:epc:id:sgtin:8901234.567895.001'

sections.markdown: ## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Missing eventID.** No dedup on replay. Compute a stable hash of event contents + partner ID.
**Mistake 2: Non-CBV bizStep values.** Custom strings break interop; use the CBV URIs.
**Mistake 3: Missing readPoint + bizLocation.** Regulators reject.
**Mistake 4: PII in event extensions.** Never.
**Mistake 5: XML EPCIS 1.x for new projects.** 2.0 JSON-LD is the modern standard; XML is legacy.
**Mistake 6: Not versioning events.** Schema evolution + regulator changes; keep event `type` + `@context` current.
**Mistake 7: Global timestamps in local timezone.** Store in UTC; `eventTimeZoneOffset` for local reference.
**Mistake 8: Central single-DB assumption.** Each party owns their events; share via query/subscribe API.
## Best practices
**1. EPCIS 2.0 JSON-LD** for new projects.
**2. Idempotent eventID** hash for replay safety.
**3. Strict CBV vocabulary** — no custom strings.
**4. All 5 dimensions (WHO/WHAT/WHEN/WHERE/WHY)** in every event.
**5. Master data separately** from events.
**6. UTC timestamps + tz offset.**
**7. Rate-limit + auth** on capture + query endpoints.
**8. Sensor payloads** via 2.0 SensorEvent extension.
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy)** — Generate a valid ObjectEvent JSON in Dart.
**Practice 2 (Medium)** — Capture endpoint: POST an event to a local EPCIS server (drift-backed).
**Practice 3 (Medium)** — Query endpoint: filter events by bizStep + time range.
**Practice 4 (Hard)** — AggregationEvent + subsequent DisaggregationEvent for a pallet.
**Practice 5 (Hard)** — Subscribe via webhook + verify HMAC signature.
**Practice 6 (Expert)** — Cross-partner event share: mock a two-party pipeline with idempotent replay + audit trail.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: What are the 5 EPCIS event types + when do you use each?**

**A:** **(1) ObjectEvent** — one or more EPCs observed at a location + time (most common; used for commissioning, shipping, receiving, dispense). **(2) AggregationEvent** — child EPCs added to a parent (SGTINs packed onto SSCC pallet). **(3) DisaggregationEvent** — child EPCs removed from a parent (pallet broken into cases). **(4) TransactionEvent** — link EPCs to a business transaction (a PO delivery confirmation, an invoice reference). **(5) TransformationEvent** — inputs consumed + outputs produced (blending, cutting, repacking; food ingredient → product). **(6) AssociationEvent (2.0)** — link two identifiers (SGTIN ↔ RFID EPC). **Each event has REQUIRED dimensions:** action (ADD/OBSERVE/DELETE), eventTime, eventTimeZoneOffset, readPoint, bizLocation, bizStep, disposition. **Interviewer signal:** knowing all 5 + when to use each shows depth.

**Q2: What is CBV + why does it matter?**

**A:** **CBV (Core Business Vocabulary)** is GS1's standardized VALUE SET for EPCIS fields — bizStep (shipping / receiving / commissioning / dispense / destroy / repacking / …), disposition (in_transit / in_progress / sold / destroyed / recalled / …), source-destination-type (owning_party / possessing_party / …), transaction-type (po / invoice / bol / …). **Why it matters:** interop. If Party A uses `shipping` + Party B uses `ship` + Party C uses `outbound` — cross-party queries can't unify. CBV forces everyone to use the same URIs. Also CBV values encode as URIs like `https://ref.gs1.org/cbv/BizStep-shipping` — self-describing + resolvable. **Trap:** using custom strings for bizStep = breaks EPCIS conformance + regulator submission. Always use CBV.

**Q3: How does EPCIS 2.0 differ from 1.x?**

**A:** **EPCIS 1.x** (~2007) — XML data format; SOAP + REST APIs; monolithic centralized repositories. **EPCIS 2.0** (2022+) — JSON-LD data format; **REST-only** API surface with clear endpoint patterns; **AssociationEvent** + **SensorEvent** extensions; cleaner schema. **Benefits:** JSON-LD parses + queries with modern tooling (Node, Python, Dart); REST endpoints are easier than SOAP; sensor + IoT-native events. **Migration path:** legacy 1.x systems still exist; adapters convert; regulators (India CDSCO) supported both during transition. **New projects → 2.0 by default**; 1.x only when integrating with a legacy partner. Interviewer bonus: knowing the SensorEvent addition.

**Q4: How would you architect cross-party event sharing?**

**A:** **(1) Each party runs an EPCIS repository** — could be a hosted service (RaphAI, Movilitas, Systech) or self-built on Postgres. **(2) Capture endpoint** — receives events from party's internal systems (POS, WMS, ERP). **(3) Query + subscribe API** — exposes events to authorized partners. **(4) Authorization** — OAuth 2.0 + scopes; a wholesaler can query events for SGTINs they own or received. **(5) Idempotency** — eventID hash prevents duplicates on retry. **(6) Rate-limit** on partner queries. **(7) Regulator submission** — dispense events pushed to CDSCO / DSCSA per regulation. **(8) Consortium hubs** in some sectors — central repository parties push to + query. **(9) Change data capture** — internal DB → EPCIS events via triggers or Kafka Connect. **The mental model** — federated event ownership + standardized interop API. Interviewer signal: not proposing a monolith.

**Q5: How would you consume EPCIS events from a Flutter app?**

**A:** **(1) Backend service** proxies EPCIS repository (never expose raw repo to mobile; add auth + caching). **(2) REST client (Dio) with typed API** — Retrofit-generated interfaces. **(3) Local cache** — Isar / drift for offline event browsing; last-N events per SGTIN. **(4) UI** — timeline view of an SGTIN's journey (scan → chain); recall dashboard; cold-chain history. **(5) FCM push** on subscribed criteria — 'when SGTIN in a recall batch is scanned anywhere, notify.' **(6) Capture flow** — worker scans SGTIN + confirms bizStep → app POSTs an ObjectEvent to the backend. **(7) Offline capture queue** — WorkManager retries when connectivity returns. **(8) Auth** — OAuth to the backend; scoped access per user role. **(9) Analytics** — event volume, capture-fail rate, sync lag. **(10) Compliance UI** — show regulator submission status per event.

**Q6: What are common performance + scale considerations?**

**A:** **Scale reality:** a global pharma brand emits ~10 events per SGTIN × billions of SGTINs = petabytes. **Design:** (1) **Time-partitioned storage** (BigQuery, Snowflake, Postgres partitioned tables). (2) **Indexes on epcList + eventTime + bizStep + bizLocation** — most queries filter these. (3) **Streaming ingest** via Kafka / Pub/Sub → materialized event store. (4) **Cold storage** for historic events (compliance retention often 7-10 years). (5) **Query optimization** — precomputed views for common queries ('latest event per SGTIN'). (6) **Rate-limits + query throttles.** (7) **Pagination + cursor** on large result sets. (8) **CDN caching** for stable historical data. (9) **Read-replica** for query traffic. (10) **Cost monitoring** — compliance data explodes if not partitioned + tiered. Interviewer signal: knowing this is a data-engineering problem, not just an API.

## Real-world usage

- **Pharma track-and-trace** — CDSCO / DSCSA / EU FMD.
- **Cold chain** — vaccines + biologics.
- **Food safety** — farm-to-fork.
- **Anti-counterfeit** — luxury + medical.
- **Retail Sunrise 2027** — consumer trace via Digital Link + EPCIS backends.
- **NOT ideal for** — low-value FMCG (batch trace enough); non-serialized goods.

## Advanced notes

- **@context** — JSON-LD context anchoring vocabulary.
- **CBV URIs** — `https://ref.gs1.org/cbv/…`.
- **EQL (EPCIS Query Language)** — subset of query params for filtering.
- **Master Data (MD)** — separate REST endpoint for GLN / product / party metadata.
- **Subscribe schedules** — immediate / periodic / cron.
- **Sensor Element (2.0)** — attaches temperature / humidity / other readings.
- **Error codes** — 400 for validation, 404 for missing, 401 for unauthorized.
- **Standard REST paths** — /capture /events /eventTypes /queries /subscriptions /vocabularies.
- **JSON Schema** — 2.0 ships with a schema for validation.
- **Extension attributes** — beyond CBV, custom `bizStepExt` etc. discouraged for interop.
- **Time series analytics** — Grafana / Superset dashboards on the event repository.
- **Regulator connectors** — CDSCO submission format is a superset of standard EPCIS.
